logline: A star surgeon and an ambitious junior doctor become entangled in a pharmaceutical company's illegal human drug trials preying on the rural poor - a medical thriller built on institutional rot.

bollymeter.basis: A 7.6 IMDb rating reflects audience appreciation of Shefali Shah's performance in a show critics found overambitious - Film Companion's Rahul Desai argued it bites off more than it can chew, and the high-on-films.com review called it a hasty thriller; the subject matter is important but the execution is cluttered.

pull_quotes.text: Human bites off more than it can chew.

seasons.review_body: Human arrived on Disney+ Hotstar on January 14, 2022 - a ten-episode medical thriller co-directed by Vipul Amrutlal Shah and Mozez Singh, exposing the machinery of unethical pharmaceutical drug trials conducted on vulnerable rural patients. The subject matter is both urgent and under-explored in Indian popular fiction. IMDb audiences rated it 7.6/10, making it the most-searched Indian web series in the first half of 2022 according to IMDb's own data. Critics split on execution. Film Companion's review argued the show is overloaded - too many characters, too many plot threads, and dialogue that strains under expository pressure. Bollywood Life praised it as mysterious, murky and magnificent. The consensus sits at a genuine performance-versus-writing tension: Shefali Shah's Dr. Gauri Nath is complex and committed, Kirti Kulhari's junior doctor arc is credibly observed, but the ten-episode structure frequently sacrifices coherence for shock. The drug-trial subject matter alone makes it worth one watch.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere drops both leads into the hospital system at different altitudes - Shah as the commanding department head, Kulhari as the aspirant who needs her patronage. The pharmaceutical subplot is introduced early and the socioeconomic stakes are established without sentimentality.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first glimpse of what Vayu Pharma's trial patients actually look like - a visual argument the show makes before it makes a verbal one.
